title: The Thing in the Floodway
hook: After three nights of hard rain, people start vanishing near drainage tunnels, pump houses, and underpasses.
truth: A parasitic water-spirit called the River Husk has nested in the floodway infrastructure and is hollowing out living hosts to make a path inland.

monster.name: The River Husk
monster.instinct: To hollow out living hosts and return them to the water system.
weaknesses: dry ground consecrated by living memory

countdown.label: First Sign
countdown.text: A dog refuses to cross a puddle under the floodway overpass, then begins growling at the storm drain.

countdown.label: First Loss
countdown.text: A maintenance worker misses checkout after inspecting a pump alarm.

countdown.label: False Return
countdown.text: The missing worker is seen at home, soaked through, smiling without recognizing family.

countdown.label: System Shift
countdown.text: Water begins flowing uphill through a sealed drainage channel.

countdown.label: Public Crisis
countdown.text: Basements across a low neighbourhood flood from the drains upward.

countdown.label: Final Breach
countdown.text: Every storm drain in the district opens at once and the River Husk calls its hosts home.

clues.text: Muddy water stands inside a locked basement with no broken pipes.
A victim's phone plays thick static only when held near standing water.
Salt crystals cling to a storm drain grate that city maps say should be dry.
Names of old drowning victims appear in condensation on tunnel concrete.
A returned victim exhales damp air that smells of river weeds.
A memorial bench near the underpass stays bone dry in the rain.

keeperHints: Let the mystery begin with municipal inconvenience before it becomes supernatural.
Use wet footprints, wrong water levels, and bad radio calls as pressure.
The River Husk should feel local, practical, and old, not cosmic.
revealPolicy: Reveal the water-spirit through traces, hosts, and impossible infrastructure before naming it.
automationSafety: Do not declare a player character drowned or possessed without explicit consent.
Do not solve the weakness unless the group earns the names-and-salt connection.
